subject: ventures/json-ld-rich-result-validator
auditor: agent session (Claude), round 78, see run record
professional: a technical SEO who validates structured data daily against Google Search Central's per-feature docs and the Rich Results Test; first checks: required vs recommended properties per rich-result type, whether nested and @graph/@id-linked entities are found, and whether 'eligible' matches what the Rich Results Test would say

evidence.correctness: Ran 20 probe inputs through validate() (scratchpad probe p.mjs, `node p.mjs`). Right: price '$12.50'/'1,200' rejected, Product needs name plus one of offers/review/aggregateRating, Breadcrumb last item may omit item, VideoObject name/thumbnailUrl/uploadDate required, FAQ Aug-2023 note, AggregateOffer lowPrice accepted. Wrong: SoftwareApplication with only offers, or only aggregateRating and no price, both report eligible:true errors:0, while Google's Software App doc requires name AND offers.price AND one of aggregateRating/review; @type ['Organization','LocalBusiness'] with no address reports eligible:true (first-match dispatch), reversed order reports the address error; '2026-13-45' passes the date check (Python datetime.date.fromisoformat raises 'month must be in 1..12'); schema.org ItemAvailability values MadeToOrder and Reserved are flagged as unrecognised; Yoast-style @graph author {'@id':...} gets a false 'Author is missing name'. Google docs and schema.org were unreachable from this session (developers.google.com ENOTFOUND, schema.org proxy 403), so the Google rules are cited from the auditor's knowledge of the published pages, not a fresh fetch.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked end to end: 11 rule sets present (Product, Article+subtypes, LocalBusiness+34 subtypes, Organization, Recipe, Event, JobPosting, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, SoftwareApplication, VideoObject); @graph flattened (probe 'yoast'); HTML extraction incl. type with '; charset' attribute; 5 builders produce zero-error markup (calc.test.mjs); CSV export with formula guard; usage opt-out and disclaimer on page (page.test.mjs). Gap against the README's own words: 'finds every structured-data entity' but nested entities (WebPage.mainEntity Product) are never checked (probe 'nested': only WebPage reported).
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: tests 30, pass 30, fail 0 (~0.1 s). 5 seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (Breadcrumb last-item rule, price regex), 3 survived (VideoObject thumbnailUrl error->warning, aggregateRating ratingCount&&reviewCount -> ||, VirtualLocation url check disabled). No test covers VideoObject, VirtualLocation, aggregateRating counts, multi-type nodes or @id references.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (313 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html. Pure functions, no deps, < escaped in builder output, CSV formula guard. Defects: ruleFor() dispatches on the first type that has a rule so multi-typed nodes are order-dependent (calc.mjs:223); getPath() silently reads only the first array element; @context check is a substring regex (calc.mjs:244, 'https://evil.example/schema.org' passes); reportCsv body mis-indented; long one-line rule bodies hard to review.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, 'not affiliated with Google', 'cannot promise what Google will show', and the FAQ 2023 limit are present and accurate (index.html:64,102,112,124). Not backed: README.md:4 'finds every structured-data entity' (nested ones are not found); index.html meta/README 'every missing required ... property' and index.html:64 'against Google's published requirements' are contradicted for SoftwareApplication (offers.price and rating/review rules wrong) and Product review subproperties are unchecked. The page's own SoftwareApplication JSON-LD (index.html:11) has no aggregateRating/review, so by Google's doc it is not rich-result eligible, yet page.test.mjs asserts it validates with 0 errors.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: paste a WordPress/Yoast page (graph with @id refs) -> spurious author warning; paste a product page that nests Product under WebPage/ItemList -> nothing checked; paste an app landing page -> told eligible when Google would not show the snippet. A technical SEO would hit at least one of these in the first hour and fall back to the Rich Results Test. Useful as a draft-markup linter and starter generator for flat single-entity blocks.
evidence.domain: Compared with Google Search Central per-feature docs (Product snippet, Software App, Article, Event, JobPosting, Breadcrumb, Video, Recipe, LocalBusiness, FAQ change of Aug 2023) and schema.org (ItemAvailability, multiple @type semantics) plus ISO 8601. Matches on most required/recommended splits; departs on SoftwareApplication eligibility, Review snippet requirements (review.author, reviewRating) not modelled, retired ~110-char headline limit still warned, ItemAvailability list incomplete, ISO 8601 decimal-fraction durations (PT1.5H) rejected, no nested-entity or @id resolution which the Rich Results Test does.

defects.what: SoftwareApplication eligibility rule is wrong: it accepts any one of offers/aggregateRating/review, while Google requires offers.price AND one of aggregateRating or review. Apps with only a price, or only a rating, are reported eligible:true with 0 errors
Multi-typed nodes dispatch to the first type with a rule, so ['Organization','LocalBusiness'] skips the LocalBusiness required-address check (result depends on array order)
Nested entities (WebPage.mainEntity Product, ItemList items, Product inside Offer graphs) are never validated; README says it 'finds every structured-data entity'
@id node references inside @graph are not resolved, so Yoast/Rank Math markup with author {"@id":...} gets a false 'Author is missing name' warning
Core rules untested: 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive (VideoObject required thumbnailUrl, aggregateRating count rule, VirtualLocation url)
README and page claim 'every missing required property' and 'Google's published requirements'; contradicted by the SoftwareApplication rule and unchecked Review snippet properties
The page's own SoftwareApplication JSON-LD lacks aggregateRating/review (not eligible per Google) and page.test.mjs asserts it passes with 0 errors
Product review / Review snippet requirements (review.author, review.reviewRating.ratingValue) not checked; an empty review object makes a Product eligible
ItemAvailability allow-list misses MadeToOrder and Reserved, producing false warnings
ISO_DATE is shape-only: 2026-13-45 passes; also accepts a space separator
ISO_DURATION rejects valid decimal-fraction durations such as PT1.5H
Headline >110 characters warning reflects a retired (AMP-era) limit; Google's current Article doc gives no character cap
jobLocationType given as an array ['TELECOMMUTE'] is not recognised, producing a false jobLocation error
@context check is a substring regex, so any URL containing 'schema.org' (https://evil.example/schema.org) passes
LocalBusiness subtype list is a hand-picked 34; common subtypes (ClothingStore, Attorney, MedicalClinic, AutoBodyShop) fall through to 'no rich result checked'

verdict: A tidy, dependency-free linter whose flat-entity rules for Product, Breadcrumb, Video, Recipe, JobPosting and FAQ mostly match Google's docs, with an accurate FAQ-2023 note and a working builder. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and verification: SoftwareApplication eligibility is wrong in both directions (the tool's own page markup is called eligible when Google's rules say it is not), multi-typed nodes are checked order-dependently, nested and @id-linked entities (the normal shape of Yoast/Rank Math output) are missed or mis-flagged, and 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive. Google Search Central and schema.org were unreachable from this session, so Google rules are cited from the published docs as known, not freshly fetched.
